title: Does Q&A Boost Engagement? Health Messaging Experiments in the United States and Ghana
eligible_reason: The paper reports preregistered randomized field experiments (Ghana and Michigan SMS messaging, plus a social-media ad experiment) comparing Q&A-style with direct-statement messages; outcomes are cross-sectional information-seeking and self-reported behaviour by arm. No staggered adoption. PACKAGE MISMATCH: the archive stored for this DOI (_archive_mnsc.2024.04405.zip, readme dated 2025-07-19) is the replication package for 'Base Rate Neglect as a Source of Inaccurate Statistical Discrimination' by Hagmann, Sajons and Tinsley (online hiring experiments, lm(choice ~ condition * sample) in man/manuscript.qmd), not for the Kirgios et al. paper. Neither paper has an eligible design.
design_notes: Package content: statisticalDiscrimination.Rproj, man/manuscript.qmd (Quarto manuscript with inline R), data/hiring_study_{gender,neutral,race,infochoice}.Rds, Qualtrics .qsf files and AsPredicted PDFs for four hiring experiments; all regressions are lm() of hiring choice on condition x sample with optional participant/candidate controls. The frame's 'ft_staggered' flag for the Q&A paper is a false positive (likely 'staggered' message timing in the SMS design).
n_adoption_cohorts_note: No staggered binary adoption in the reported designs.
data_files: data/hiring_raw.Rds, hiring_study_gender.Rds, hiring_study_infochoice.Rds, hiring_study_neutral.Rds, hiring_study_race.Rds, simulations.Rds (for the WRONG paper)
data_files_note: Data files present belong to the Hagmann-Sajons-Tinsley statistical-discrimination package, not to the Q&A messaging paper. The correct supplement for 10.1287/mnsc.2024.04405 should be re-downloaded if this paper is ever needed.
screener_notes: Screened from package only. ACTION FOR LEAD: package_dir ~/did_packages/mnsc/mnsc.2024.04405 holds the wrong replication package (title in readme.rtf: 'Base Rate Neglect as a Source of Inaccurate Statistical Discrimination'); the archive itself is mismatched, so the download/DOI mapping should be checked. Eligibility verdict (not eligible) holds for both papers since both are RCTs without staggered adoption.
